radiusSource: Radius 0.677 Jupiter radii from the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated radius (its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, since 55 Cnc f does not transit (https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html): 48,400.1 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.1526 +/- 0.0088 Jupiter masses (Moutou et al. (2026), A&A 705, A190, Table 3: minimum mass (m sin i) 48.5 +/- 2.8 Earth masses from the star's radial velocities; at the assumed tilt of 93.9 degrees the mass is 0.2% more, https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11523) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.
orbitalPeriodSource: Moutou et al. (2026), A&A 705, A190, Table 3, a fit of the star's radial velocities, for the period, eccentricity, argument, time of conjunction and semi-major axis (a/R* is its 0.802 au over the star's recorded 656,045 km). The tilt and node are NOT measured for this planet: they are assumed equal to those Xiao et al. (2026, arXiv:2609.01377) measure for 55 Cnc d (https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11523): P 260.58 d

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius in the shared neutral gray. No image, color, map or oblateness of 55 Cnc f is measured; only its size, mass and orbit are.

massSource: 0.1526 Jupiter masses: Moutou et al. (2026), A&A 705, A190, Table 3: minimum mass (m sin i) 48.5 +/- 2.8 Earth masses from the star's radial velocities; at the assumed tilt of 93.9 degrees the mass is 0.2% more (https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11523).
